title: Housekeeping Room Inspection from Photos
summary: Check each cleaned room from attendant photos against your room standard: bed, bathroom, amenities, minibar and visible damage, with supervisors confirming before the room is released.

seo.title: Housekeeping Room Inspection from Photos | VipraTech
seo.description: Computer vision that checks housekeeping photos against room standards for bed, bathroom, amenities and damage, so supervisors focus where it matters.

problem.intro: Every departure room should be inspected before it is released for sale, but on a day with many check-outs and early arrivals, supervisors cannot walk every room. A missing towel, a used glass, hair in the shower or a stain on the linen then reaches a guest, and often a review.

pain_points.title: Too many rooms to inspect
pain_points.detail: Supervisors cover several floors and prioritise early arrivals, so many rooms are released on the attendant's word.

pain_points.title: Standards that vary by attendant
pain_points.detail: New and temporary staff set amenities and fold towels differently from the standard, especially in peak season.

pain_points.title: Damage found by the next guest
pain_points.detail: Broken fittings, stained carpets or missing items are discovered after check-in rather than reported to maintenance.

pain_points.title: No record of what was checked
pain_points.detail: When a guest complains, there is no evidence of the room's condition at release.

solution.overview: We build a room inspection flow in a phone app that housekeeping already carries. After cleaning, the attendant takes photos from a short set of fixed angles for the room type: bed, bathroom, vanity, amenities tray, minibar and floor. Vision models check each photo against your standard, for example bed made with the correct linen and cushions, towels and amenities present and placed, no visible stains or litter, minibar stocked and nothing left behind. Rooms that pass with high confidence get a light supervisor check; failures and uncertain photos go to the supervisor with the exact issue marked. Damage creates a maintenance ticket, and the PMS room status changes only after supervisor sign-off.
capabilities: Guided photo capture per room type with fixed angles
Checks for bed making, towels, amenities placement and minibar stock
Detection of visible stains, litter, used items and items left behind
Damage spotting for fittings, furniture and soft furnishings, with maintenance tickets
Supervisor queue prioritised by failures, uncertainty and arrival times
Room condition record at release for complaint handling and coaching

workflow.title: Capture after cleaning
workflow.detail: The attendant photographs the room from the fixed angles defined for that room type.

workflow.title: Check against the standard
workflow.detail: Vision models compare each photo with the room standard and score each item.

workflow.title: Decide the route
workflow.detail: Passing rooms go to a light check, and failed or uncertain items go to the supervisor with the issue marked.

workflow.title: Supervisor inspection
workflow.detail: The supervisor confirms or corrects the result, physically for flagged rooms, and the attendant fixes any issues.

workflow.title: Release and log
workflow.detail: After sign-off the PMS room status updates to inspected, and photos are stored with the room record.

workflow.title: Report and coach
workflow.detail: Weekly reports show recurring misses by item and floor for training.

inputs: Photos from fixed angles after cleaning
Room standards and reference photos per room type
Room status and arrivals list from the PMS
outputs: Item-by-item result per room with photo evidence
PMS room status updates after sign-off
Weekly misses by item, floor and shift
human_in_the_loop: Supervisors sign off every room before it is released and physically inspect all flagged rooms. Results are used for coaching, and any disciplinary step stays with the executive housekeeper and HR.
integrations: Hotel PMS for room status and arrivals
Housekeeping apps or WhatsApp for task alerts
Quality audit dashboards for hotel groups
guardrails: Photos taken only in vacant rooms after check-out, never with guests or their belongings in frame
Room status changes only after supervisor sign-off
Confidence shown for each item, and uncertain items never auto-pass
Results not used for automatic penalties
Reference standards updated whenever room design or amenities change
compliance_notes: Photo capture is limited to vacant rooms so guest privacy is not affected.
Staff are told how photos and results are used, in line with DPDP Act 2023 notice and purpose principles.

pilot.scope: Departure rooms of one or two room types on selected floors of one property, with supervisors inspecting every room as usual so results can be compared.
deliverables: Room standards and capture angles for the pilot room types
Models tuned on your rooms and amenities
Supervisor queue and PMS status flow

what_we_measure.how: Model results compared with the supervisor's physical inspection of the same rooms.
Issues found by supervisors or guests in rooms the model passed.
Inspection time for passed and flagged rooms, compared with inspections before the pilot.
Count of repeat issues by item and floor across the pilot weeks.

faqs.a: No. It helps supervisors focus on the rooms and items that need attention and gives them evidence. Every room is still signed off by a supervisor.
Usually not. The app runs on the phones or shared devices housekeeping already uses, and capture takes a short sequence of photos per room.

faqs.q: Can it spot hair or small stains?
faqs.a: Larger stains, litter, missing items and misplaced amenities are detected more reliably than single hairs. Small-detail checks such as hair in the shower stay on the supervisor's checklist for flagged and sampled rooms.
We recommend starting with departure rooms. Stayover rooms contain guests' belongings, so photo capture there needs a separate policy and is usually limited or excluded.
